processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heating stage of the hot-compression schedule.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 1150 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at 1150 °C so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression at 1 s^-1 to 60% (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.

structures.overall_structure: After 60% hot compression at 1150 °C and 1 s^-1 the deformation-zone microstructures differ: zone 1 (difficult deformation) consists of large grains, whereas zones 2 (small deformation) and 3 (large deformation) consist of uniform equiaxed dynamically recrystallized grains that appear coarser than those formed at 1050 °C/1 s^-1. The DRX volume fraction increases with temperature, and the recrystallized grain size grows significantly as temperature rises.

microstructure_list.region: Zone 1 - difficult deformation zone (top and bottom centre near loading surfaces)
Zone 2 - small deformation zone (left and right ends adjacent to the horizontal centre line)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Uniform equiaxed recrystallized grains, appearing coarser than at 1050 °C/1 s^-1

microstructure_list.region: Zone 3 - large deformation zone (central band / core of the compressed sample)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Uniform equiaxed recrystallized grains, appearing coarser than at 1050 °C/1 s^-1; DRX is more complete in the large-deformation zone

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to 60% (maximum true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricants affixed to both end faces; heated to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s, homogenized 120 s, cooled to 1150 °C at 5 °C/s, held 15 s before compression, water-spray quenched after.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Fine and uniform DRX grain structure; the 1150 °C/1 s^-1 condition lies outside the recommended fine-grain windows

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; ground, polished and etched with 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction); micrographs with 100 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the initial microstructure and the microstructure evolution in the three deformation zones after hot compression
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 1150 °C/1 s^-1 sample (figure_009 panel f): zone 1 shows large grains, zones 2 and 3 show uniform equiaxed recrystallized grains that appear coarser than at 1050 °C/1 s^-1.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 1150 °C, ε̇ = 1 s^-1, 60% compression (true strain 0.92), cylindrical Φ8 mm × 12 mm sample
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the rheological/flow stress behaviour and construct constitutive/DRX models
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; the flow stress curve of this condition exhibits a peak followed by softening.

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis with Zener-Hollomon parameter; linear regression fitting
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The fitted straight lines in Fig. 4 show poor parallelism, indicating the deformation conditions significantly affect the activation energy; the calculated value is therefore only the average over the experimental range.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate peak stress, temperature and strain rate to determine the DRX activation energy
analytical_models.model_note: Activation energy computed as Q_p = 1000·R·k1·k2; applicable to the whole steel over 900-1150 °C and 0.01-10 s^-1.

analytical_models.equation_role: Characterize the combined influence of T and strain rate on rheological stress
analytical_models.model_note: Z = ε̇ exp(Q_p/RT); lnZ for this sample (1150 °C, 1 s^-1) is 56.62 (Table 1).

computational_details.simulation_method: Cingara-McQueen equation and multiple linear regression to relate DRX characteristic values (εc/σc, εp/σp, εs/σs) to lnZ
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: εc/εp ≈ 0.452, similar to literature values obtained from the θ-σ inflection-point method, indicating the method is reliable.

analytical_models.equation_role: Determine the material constant C and the critical strain for DRX
Express critical, peak and steady-state stress/strain as functions of lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Regression fits R between 0.911 and 0.957; applicable to the whole steel over the studied T and ε̇ ranges.

computational_details.simulation_method: Finite element (DEFORM-3D) setup with Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm for mathematical regression of DRX average grain size
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid plastic body and die indenter as a rigid body; material parameters given to the die; semi-symmetric specimen model; friction of the billet-die contact interface set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient between billet and air set to 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation in line with the thermal compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% for all samples; absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size mostly within 3 µm.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict DRX average grain size as a function of strain rate and temperature

unmapped_findings: Zener-Hollomon parameter for this sample (1150 °C, 1 s^-1): lnZ = 56.62 (Table 1). Table 1 reports lnZ decreasing with increasing T and increasing with strain rate across 900-1150 °C and 0.01-10 s^-1.

Dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel Q_p = 669.844 kJ mol^-1, determined from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine function equation with k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690 and α = 0.00599; this is only an average value over the experimental range because the fitted lines show poor parallelism.

The DRX average grain size of the steel increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; the study reports that at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 (not this sample) the grain size exceeds 70 µm, indicating rapid recrystallized grain growth.

Recommended hot-working windows for a fine and uniform grain structure: 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 and 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1; the 1150 °C/1 s^-1 condition of this sample lies outside these fine-grain windows.

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature lowers the peak/flow stress. Peak stress at 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1 (not this sample) is 53.8 MPa.

No direct numeric peak stress, hardness, tensile or grain-size value is reported for the specific 1150 °C/1 s^-1 condition; only qualitative zone-resolved microstructures (figure_009 panel f) are provided for this sample.

The compression experiments used mica foils with high-temperature lubricants on both end faces to reduce friction and non-uniform deformation; the same batch/composition confirmed reproducibility under identical conditions.
